verdict.rationale: Grafana's docs emphasize open-source data portability and avoiding vendor lock-in: OpenTelemetry integration explicitly says it protects users 'from vendor lock-in and ensuring data portability' (grafana-docs-38), Tempo supports open tracing protocols like Jaeger/Zipkin/OTel (grafana-docs-37), and dashboards/data sources can be defined as version-controlled code via provisioning and observability-as-code (grafana-docs-2, grafana-docs-3, grafana-docs-16, grafana-docs-26), enabling config export. However, there is no explicit documentation of a comprehensive 'export all my data' feature or migration tooling for bulk telemetry data itself (data typically lives in external stores like Prometheus/Loki, not Grafana), and community threads raise AGPLv3 licensing concerns that could complicate reuse (grafana-comm-9, grafana-comm-10) without directly disputing export capability. Missing for 10: explicit bulk data/dashboard export API or CLI documentation, independent hands-on confirmation of a full data-portability workflow, and clarity on how core telemetry data (not just configs) can be extracted.
